Great call using M365 — it's the right tool for a work context. Here are the three realistic options, ordered from most to least automated:

---

### Option A — Excel Online + Microsoft Graph API *(Recommended)*
**How it works:** Your Apps Script equivalent in M365 is **Office Scripts** (TypeScript, runs inside Excel Online) + **Power Automate** to schedule it. The script writes KPI rows into an Excel file stored in **OneDrive or SharePoint**. The KPI Tracker app then reads that file on demand via the **Microsoft Graph API**.

| Pros | Cons |
|---|---|
| Fully automated — no manual steps | Requires registering an Azure AD app (one-time, ~10 min) |
| Real-time data always available | Needs a Client ID + Client Secret from Azure portal |
| Familiar Excel interface for editing | Office Scripts requires M365 Business/Enterprise plan |
| Works with existing propertymax.ai scraping logic | |

**What you'd need to provide:** Azure App Client ID + Client Secret (I'll walk you through it step by step).

---

### Option B — Power Automate Webhook *(No Azure App needed)*
**How it works:** Power Automate has a built-in **"When an HTTP request is received"** trigger that gives you a public URL. You set up a flow that runs on a schedule, calls propertymax.ai (or reads from Excel), and POSTs the data directly to the KPI Tracker's API endpoint.

| Pros | Cons |
|---|---|
| No Azure AD app registration needed | Power Automate flow setup is more manual |
| Uses your existing M365 login | HTTP trigger requires Power Automate Premium ($15/mo) or P2 plan |
| Can call propertymax.ai directly | |

---

### Option C — Manual CSV Upload *(Simplest, no automation)*
**How it works:** You export the KPI data from Excel as a CSV and upload it to the KPI Tracker via a drag-and-drop interface in the Admin panel.

| Pros | Cons |
|---|---|
| Zero setup — works immediately | Manual step required each time |
| No credentials needed | Not real-time |
| Good for testing the dashboard first | |

Ask Rent is pulled directly from **PropertyMax.ai** — specifically from the `getsummary` endpoint at `https://propertymax.ai/vacancy.cfc`. Here is the exact flow:

**Source:** `propertymax.ai/vacancy.cfc?method=getsummary&regionid=<1–4>`

The scraper calls this endpoint (once per region, 4 regions total), which returns an HTML page containing summary tables. It then parses those tables with Cheerio (an HTML parser):

| Table type | Ask Rent column |
|---|---|
| Vacant / Unleased (has "Mov Out", no "Mov In") | Column 8 (index 7) of each row |
| Vacant / Preleased (has both "Mov Out" and "Mov In") | Column 9 (index 8) of each row |

The value is read as raw text from that cell, stripped of commas, and converted to a float with `parseFloat(...)`. If the cell is empty or non-numeric, it falls back to `0` — which is why "Not set" appears when PropertyMax.ai hasn't populated that field for a unit.

**In short: the Ask Rent shown in the dashboard is exactly what PropertyMax.ai stores for each unit.** If it's blank in PropertyMax.ai, it will show "Not set" here. The only way to populate it is to enter the value directly in PropertyMax.ai on the unit's detail page.
